title: lebre: online forecasting with statistically tested structural changes
description:
Installable Python library implementing LEBRE v0.55, an online one-step-ahead forecaster for a target driven by exogenous inputs, at a counted cost per step. It has three layers: a structural core whose structural changes, removals included, are accepted only when an anytime-valid e-process of predictive improvement crosses a level set by an online multiple-testing rule, with each input tested against the core forecast (which already contains the target's own past) and an innovation structure that carries accepted inputs to the forecast of integrated targets; M1, a precision expert combined with the core by AdaHedge, which sleeps while it carries no weight and wakes by evidence; and M2, which starts the output from a declared trivial reference and combines two paths by an (A,B)-Prod. With anchored=False it is LEBRE v0.54 (lebre 0.3.0); earlier versions remain available through switches.

LEBRE v0.55 was promoted by a pre-registered binding rule in the research record (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23443154; https://github.com/Iquitim/lebre-research): on 84 reserved series no family was worse than v0.54 beyond the margin (ratio 0.993 to 1.008), placebo random-walk inputs ended in the structure on 0 of 84 series (v0.54: 4 of 84) and the median per-series cost was 0.989 of v0.54's. In the reference environment (Windows, CPython 3.11, NumPy 2.2.5) its forecasts are bit-for-bit identical to the frozen research code.

Scope and limits. One-step forecasting; on basins, a small significant loss against v0.54 and a recursive-least-squares ARX of the same cost class is better; the gain on integrated series was shown on synthetic data only; weak real relations are registered as structure more slowly; the cycle must be declared; no formal guarantee in the original scale for M1 and M2; no component is original. See the research record for the full evidence and its limits.
